solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Don't hit girl

definitions.meaning: to fail to hit a target
The title for an unmarried girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A plea not to strike a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss works as a verb for failing to strike and as a noun for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Northern people in university computing

parts.note: taken as written
IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: Arctic folk studying computer science at college.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

clue.text: Strike means deduction from pay

definitions.meaning: a halt in work by employees, a strike
amounts withheld from wages, such as tax

explanation.surface: Industrial action costs workers money from their wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is both a work halt by staff and a sum withheld from a payslip.

clue.text: Like some of Bach's music, full of runs and economical

indicators.note: the music word is filled with the runs letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bach wrote many fugues, so his music can be fugal
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A description of a Baroque composition that is packed with rapid passages yet sparing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks musical here, the quick scales a keyboard player plays, but it is the cricket scoring abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal means careful and sparing with money or resources, hence thrifty.

clue.text: Tin on top of long grass

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A metal can left sitting on tall meadow vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the meadow plant but is the slang verb or noun for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a grass is an informer, the same as a snitch who tells on others.

clue.text: Part of school I arrange for storyteller

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher organises a section of the school day for a visiting author.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for storyteller' as the definition; 'for' is only a link word, so the definition is 'storyteller' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for lying, so a storyteller can be a fibber.

clue.text: Radios covering end of nasty dictatorships

indicators.note: the radios word wraps around the extra letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: trannies is old British slang for transistor radios

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word nasty is taken

explanation.surface: Wireless sets blanketing the airwaves around some unpleasant event, ruling regimes.
explanation.walkthrough: TRANNIES is dated British slang for transistor radios.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyranny is a state ruled by a cruel absolute ruler, which is what a dictatorship is.

clue.text: How erotic is a sauna?

parts.note: a sauna is literally full of vapour, and the same adjective means sexy or racy

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about how sexy a sauna is.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a racy scene is the same word that literally describes a vapour-filled room, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both sexually charged and full of hot vapour, as a sauna is.

clue.text: Total love for wrestling

parts.note: a sum is a total
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Complete devotion to grappling as a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the traditional Japanese form of wrestling between heavy competitors.

clue.text: Call for artist to produce exciting work

parts.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager
J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A summons for a painter to create something thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: TURNER is J. M. W. Turner, the celebrated English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book is called a page-turner because readers cannot stop reading it.

clue.text: A short distance dogs perhaps returned

indicators.note: returned means the pets word is read backwards

parts.note: dogs are an example of household pets

explanation.surface: Animals coming back from a brief walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace, so it covers only a short way.

clue.text: There is no variation in any case

definitions.meaning: if things are ..., they do not differ at all

explanation.surface: A statement that nothing differs at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both identical throughout and nevertheless, in spite of everything.

clue.text: A gentle knocking in bathroom fitting

definitions.meaning: a faucet on a basin or bath

explanation.surface: A soft rattling noise coming from the plumbing in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap is a light rap on a door and also the valve that releases water at a sink.

clue.text: Warden puts on a stone; I don't recognise him

indicators.note: in a down clue the warden word is put under the stone, so the stone comes first

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for a stone in weight
a ranger is a warden of a park or forest

explanation.surface: A park keeper gains fourteen pounds and becomes unrecognisable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on a stone' reads as gaining weight; ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is someone you do not know, so you would not recognise that person.

clue.text: Warning that waiter will get nothing?

definitions.meaning: a piece of advance warning or secret information
read whimsically, the tip is off, so no gratuity is left for the server

explanation.surface: An alert that the restaurant staff will be left without a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is advance confidential information, and read literally means the gratuity is cancelled.

clue.text: Pipe organ I played for two children

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone performed on a church instrument for a pair of youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: A pigeon pair is a British expression for a family's one boy and one girl, or boy-girl twins.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a pair of offspring, a son and a daughter, especially twins.

clue.text: What baby needs is to sleep with family

indicators.note: with puts the second piece alongside the first

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly
kin are relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: An infant's requirement is a snooze among relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What baby needs' looks like sleep, but it is the definition: a napkin is the formal word for a nappy, or diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Napkin is the full form of nappy, the absorbent cloth an infant wears.

clue.text: Problem in a rising display of hostility

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the words are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A difficulty growing in a show of aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or animosity, a hostile attitude towards someone.

clue.text: A container is not closed

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A pot that has been left unsealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajar describes a door slightly open, which is to say not shut.

clue.text: Ranch of Ron's regularly provides fruit

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A farm belonging to Ron yields produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The acorn is the nut, botanically the fruit, of the oak tree.

clue.text: Starting a baby is the idea

explanation.surface: A suggestion that having a child is the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Conception means both becoming pregnant and the forming of a notion in the mind.

clue.text: Worry, being mixed race

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of race are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Concern about being of mixed ethnic heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: Care can mean anxiety or concern, as in cares of the world.

clue.text: Cultivate grand argument

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a row is a quarrel, an argument

explanation.surface: Encourage a magnificent dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow plants is to raise them, which is cultivating them.

clue.text: Endurance of ill-fitting red outfit

indicators.note: an outfit that fits badly is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The stamina needed to wear a scarlet costume that doesn't fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortitude is courage in bearing pain or adversity, a form of staying power.

clue.text: Controlled temperature in tirade

parts.note: to run a business is to control it, so ran

explanation.surface: A furious outburst about thermostat settings.
explanation.definitionFit: A rant is a long angry speech, the same as a tirade.
